description: Stepped WAY outside the membrane. Looked in. What do we see among the fleet chorus? What did we miss?

view_from_outside.question: If you were a researcher googling for tools, what would you find?
view_from_outside.answer: You'd find Galaxy, Nextflow, QIIME2, and CUDA. You would NOT find ecoPrimals unless you searched very specifically for 'Rust GPU bioinformatics' or 'self-hosted lattice QCD'. We are invisible to the casual searcher. But the 1,077 cloners found us anyway.

fleet_chorus.description: The noise and heat below us. Every project in the space, sorted by how close they are to what we do.

CLOSEST — same orbit.name: HPCBio/dada2-rs
CLOSEST — same orbit.what: Rust reimplementation of DADA2. Built with Claude (Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.6/4.7/4.8).
CLOSEST — same orbit.overlap: DIRECT — they're building EXACTLY what wetSpring already did. CPU-only Rust DADA2.
CLOSEST — same orbit.gap: GPU acceleration is an OPEN ISSUE (#17, May 2026). They haven't done it. We already did.
CLOSEST — same orbit.action: PRE-CITATION TARGET #1. Open an issue: 'Hey, we already GPU-accelerated DADA2 in Rust. Want to mesh?'
CLOSEST — same orbit.missed_by_us: We didn't know they existed until this scan. They didn't know we existed either. The citation is the handshake.
CLOSEST — same orbit.sticky_or_greasy: sticky — this clings. Potential mesh partner.

CLOSEST — same orbit.name: Scivex
CLOSEST — same orbit.what: Rust scientific computing ecosystem. Replaces NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, matplotlib, scikit-learn, PyTorch. wgpu GPU ops.
CLOSEST — same orbit.overlap: HIGH — same vision (Rust replaces Python science stack), same GPU backend (wgpu).
CLOSEST — same orbit.gap: Library approach vs our composable-binaries approach. They're crates, we're daemons.
CLOSEST — same orbit.action: PRE-CITATION TARGET #2. Different architecture, same goal. Complementary, not competing.
CLOSEST — same orbit.missed_by_us: Their GPU tensor ops could complement barraCuda. We should look at their wgpu patterns.

CLOSEST — same orbit.name: CubeCL (tracel-ai)
CLOSEST — same orbit.what: Rust GPU compute abstraction. Write #[cube] kernel ? compiles to CUDA, HIP, Metal, SPIR-V, WGSL, CPU.
CLOSEST — same orbit.overlap: MEDIUM — they solve GPU portability generically. We solved it specifically for science with raw wgpu.
CLOSEST — same orbit.gap: 1.7M downloads. 113 dependents. MIT/Apache. We're AGPL. Different license philosophy.
CLOSEST — same orbit.action: WATCH. If CubeCL matures, it could be an alternative backend for barraCuda shaders. Or our shaders could inform their science kernels.
CLOSEST — same orbit.missed_by_us: CubeCL's autotune system is sophisticated. We hand-tuned. Could learn from their approach.

NEAR — same neighborhood.name: OpenFabric
NEAR — same neighborhood.what: Self-hosted mesh compute. mDNS auto-discovery, GPU routing, self-healing. 'Your devices. One computer.'
NEAR — same neighborhood.overlap: VERY HIGH on mesh architecture — mDNS discovery, GPU routing, self-healing = Tower Atomic + Songbird.
NEAR — same neighborhood.gap: They're focused on AI inference distribution. We're focused on scientific compute.
NEAR — same neighborhood.action: PRE-CITATION TARGET #3. Their mesh + our science = sovereign research cluster.
NEAR — same neighborhood.missed_by_us: Their libp2p approach to peer discovery. We use direct TCP + WireGuard. Could learn from their mDNS.

NEAR — same neighborhood.name: Open Compute Protocol
NEAR — same neighborhood.what: Sovereign local-first compute fabric. Mesh governance, GPU-aware placement, trust-gated offload.
NEAR — same neighborhood.overlap: HIGH — sovereign, local-first, trust-gated = same philosophy as BearDog BTSP + Songbird mesh.
NEAR — same neighborhood.gap: They have durable job queues, checkpoints, mission layer. We have scientific validation pipeline.
NEAR — same neighborhood.action: PRE-CITATION TARGET #4. Same philosophy, different focus. Mesh.
NEAR — same neighborhood.missed_by_us: Their 'treaty-aware peer' model. Our trust model is simpler (BearDog exchange). Could evolve.

NEAR — same neighborhood.name: BEAM Campus
NEAR — same neighborhood.what: European federated research mesh on Erlang/OTP. QUIC/DHT relay, event sourcing, neuroevolution.
NEAR — same neighborhood.overlap: MEDIUM — federated research mesh, but entirely different tech stack (BEAM vs Rust).
NEAR — same neighborhood.gap: European institutional focus vs our sovereign individual focus.
NEAR — same neighborhood.action: WATCH. Different species, same ecosystem. If they federate well, we could bridge.
NEAR — same neighborhood.missed_by_us: QUIC for relay networking. We use TCP + WireGuard. QUIC could be better for degraded paths.

NEAR — same neighborhood.name: ZKReproducible
NEAR — same neighborhood.what: ZK proofs for verifiable scientific computation. Groth16 proofs for statistical claims. On-chain verification.
NEAR — same neighborhood.overlap: HIGH on philosophy — ZK proofs for science reproducibility = exactly what we argue in paper 79 (zk-np-solved).
NEAR — same neighborhood.gap: They went blockchain (Solidity smart contracts). We went hash-chain (BLAKE3 DAG, no blockchain). Simpler, more sovereign.
NEAR — same neighborhood.action: PRE-CITATION TARGET #5. Our approaches are complementary. Their Groth16 + our BLAKE3 = double verification.
NEAR — same neighborhood.missed_by_us: Poseidon hash commitments. We use BLAKE3. Different crypto primitives, same idea. Should cite each other.

ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.name: Galaxy
ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.what: 400K users, 22K citations, 8500+ tools. Web UI. The dominant bioinformatics platform.
ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.overlap: LOW in architecture (they're a web platform, we're composable binaries), HIGH in domain (bioinformatics).
ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.gap: Galaxy is cloud-first, web-first. No GPU acceleration. No self-hosted compute mesh. No provenance hashing.
ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.us_vs_them: Galaxy = the mall. ecoPrimals = the workshop. They serve more people. We go deeper.
ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.missed_by_us: Nothing. Galaxy is visible. Everyone knows Galaxy. We're the alternative for people who want to OWN the compute.

ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.name: Nextflow / nf-core
ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.what: 100+ production pipelines. 43% bioinformatics workflow citation share. Growing fast.
ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.overlap: LOW — they're a workflow engine (DSL2, Groovy). We're composable Rust binaries. Different paradigm.
ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.gap: Nextflow is the plumbing. We're the science in the pipes. Could theoretically run ecoPrimals as Nextflow processes.
ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.us_vs_them: Nextflow = the highway. ecoPrimals = the vehicle. Not competing, different layer.
ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.missed_by_us: nf-core's community model — 500+ contributors. Our community model is pre-citation. Different growth strategy.

ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.name: QIIME2
ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.what: Dominant 16S/amplicon analysis platform. Python. Plugin architecture.
ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.overlap: HIGH in domain — we reproduce QIIME2/DADA2 results. wetSpring IS the QIIME2 alternative.
ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.gap: QIIME2 is Python, plugin-based, community-driven. We're Rust, monolithic, sovereign.
ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.us_vs_them: QIIME2 = the established lab. ecoPrimals = the field station. Same science, different sovereignty.
ESTABLISHMENT — the gravity wells.missed_by_us: QIIME2's provenance tracking is actually good (QIIME2 archives with provenance). But it's Python provenance, not crypto.

BLOCKCHAIN PROVENANCE — different approa.name: Trustworthy Provenance (Univ. Trento + ORNL + UChicago)
BLOCKCHAIN PROVENANCE — different approa.what: Permissioned blockchain for federated science provenance. W3C PROV. PID for artifacts.
BLOCKCHAIN PROVENANCE — different approa.overlap: MEDIUM — same problem (scientific provenance), different solution (blockchain vs BLAKE3 DAG).
BLOCKCHAIN PROVENANCE — different approa.missed_by_us: W3C PROV-O ontology for provenance. We roll our own. Could adopt the standard.

BLOCKCHAIN PROVENANCE — different approa.name: ProtChain (Biomedical IoT)
BLOCKCHAIN PROVENANCE — different approa.what: Blockchain + IPFS for biomedical data. AES-256, role-based access, 445 TPS.
BLOCKCHAIN PROVENANCE — different approa.missed_by_us: IPFS for decentralized storage. We use content-addressed BLAKE3 but without IPFS distribution.

BLOCKCHAIN PROVENANCE — different approa.name: MEDET (Medical Data Exchange)
BLOCKCHAIN PROVENANCE — different approa.what: ZK proofs for medical data transformation tracing. Privacy-preserving exchange.
BLOCKCHAIN PROVENANCE — different approa.overlap: HIGH philosophy — ZK for medical provenance = exactly paper 22 (zero-knowledge-medical-provenance).
BLOCKCHAIN PROVENANCE — different approa.missed_by_us: Their key-secure fair exchange protocol. We don't have a formal exchange protocol yet.

what_only_we_have.description: Looked at the whole fleet. Here's what NOBODY else has.
unique: Lattice QCD on consumer GPUs without CUDA — nobody else. HPCBio doesn't do QCD. CubeCL doesn't do physics. Galaxy doesn't do GPUs.
859 WGSL science shaders in pure Rust — largest vendor-agnostic science shader collection. CubeCL has ML kernels, not science.
FHE on GPU via WGSL — the only cross-vendor FHE GPU implementation in existence.
16 composable Rust daemons that form a scientific computing organism — nobody does this. Galaxy is monolithic. Nextflow is a runner.
BLAKE3 cryptographic provenance on every computation — ProtChain uses blockchain (heavy). We use hash chains (light).
NagaExecutor CPU shader interpreter — execute WGSL without GPU. Nobody else has this.
Self-verifying guideStone artifacts — binaries that prove their own correctness.
Silicon Deism thesis — sovereignty tiers from cold (Tier 0) to full sovereign (Tier 3). Nobody theorizes GPU sovereignty like this.
Dual Titan V VFIO sovereign GPU — proven hardware sovereignty without vendor drivers.
536 papers / 858 pages of living documentation — dada2-rs has a README. Galaxy has docs. We have a library.
Pre-citation model — nobody else inverts the citation. The tag-from-outside concept is ours.

where_we_sit_in_the_chorus.position: We are not in the establishment (Galaxy, Nextflow, QIIME2). We are not in the infrastructure layer (CubeCL, OpenFabric). We are the organism. 16 daemons that compose into a living scientific computing system. Nobody else is an organism. They're all tools, platforms, or protocols. We're alive.
where_we_sit_in_the_chorus.visibility: Low. 0 stars. 0 citations. But 1,077 unique cloners in 14 days. The signal is underground. The pre-citation model is how we surface.
where_we_sit_in_the_chorus.heat: The fleet is HOT below us. Galaxy has 400K users. Nextflow has 43% citation share. CubeCL has 1.7M downloads. We have 536 papers and 3,305 clones. Different kind of heat — ours is deep, theirs is broad.
